nodes.title: Equations of a Line in Space
points: Line through A(a) parallel to vector b: Vector equation: r = a + λ b; Cartesian equation: (x − x₁)/a = (y − y₁)/b = (z − z₁)/c.
Line passing through two points A(a) and B(b): Vector equation: r = a + λ(b − a); Cartesian equation: (x − x₁)/(x₂ − x₁) = (y − y₁)/(y₂ − y₁) = (z − z₁)/(z₂ − z₁).
Coordinates of any general point on line: (x₁ + λa, y₁ + λb, z₁ + λc).
Direction ratios of line: (a, b, c); Direction cosines: (l, m, n) = (a/√(a²+b²+c²), b/√(a²+b²+c²), c/√(a²+b²+c²)).

formulas.label: Cartesian equation (2 points)
formulas.expr: (x − x₁)/(x₂ − x₁) = (y − y₁)/(y₂ − y₁) = (z − z₁)/(z₂ − z₁)

nodes.title: Angle Between Two Lines & Conditions
points: Angle θ between lines with direction ratios (a₁, b₁, c₁) and (a₂, b₂, c₂):
cosθ = |(b₁ · b₂)| / (|b₁| |b₂|) = |a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ + c₁c₂| / [√(a₁²+b₁²+c₁²) √(a₂²+b₂²+c₂²)].
Perpendicular Lines Condition: b₁ · b₂ = 0 ⟹ a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ + c₁c₂ = 0.
Parallel Lines Condition: b₁ = k b₂ ⟹ a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂.

nodes.title: Shortest Distance Between Skew Lines
points: Skew lines: Non-parallel, non-intersecting lines in three-dimensional space (they lie in different planes).
Distance between skew lines r = a₁ + λ b₁ and r = a₂ + μ b₂:
d = |[(a₂ − a₁) · (b₁ × b₂)]| / |b₁ × b₂|.
Condition for two lines to intersect (d = 0, coplanar): (a₂ − a₁) · (b₁ × b₂) = 0 ⟹ det [[x₂−x₁, y₂−y₁, z₂−z₁], [a₁, b₁, c₁], [a₂, b₂, c₂]] = 0.
Distance between parallel lines r = a₁ + λ b and r = a₂ + μ b: d = |(a₂ − a₁) × b| / |b|.

formulas.label: Intersection condition
formulas.expr: det [[x₂−x₁, y₂−y₁, z₂−z₁], [a₁, b₁, c₁], [a₂, b₂, c₂]] = 0

nodes.title: Equations of a Plane in Space
points: Normal Form: r · n̂ = p, where n̂ is unit normal vector from origin and p is perpendicular distance from origin. Cartesian: lx + my + nz = p.
Plane through A(a) perpendicular to normal n: Vector: (r − a) · n = 0 ⟹ r · n = a · n; Cartesian: a(x − x₁) + b(y − y₁) + c(z − z₁) = 0.
General Cartesian Equation: ax + by + cz + d = 0, where (a, b, c) are direction ratios of the normal vector.
Plane through 3 non-collinear points A(a), B(b), C(c): (r − a) · [(b − a) × (c − a)] = 0 ⟹ det [[x−x₁, y−y₁, z−z₁], [x₂−x₁, y₂−y₁, z₂−z₁], [x₃−x₁, y₃−y₁, z₃−z₁]] = 0.
Intercept Form: x/a + y/b + z/c = 1.

formulas.label: Normal form
formulas.expr: r · n̂ = p ⟺ lx + my + nz = p

formulas.label: Point-normal form
formulas.expr: a(x − x₁) + b(y − y₁) + c(z − z₁) = 0

nodes.title: Angle Between Planes & Distance from Point
points: Angle θ between planes r · n₁ = d₁ and r · n₂ = d₂:
cosθ = |n₁ · n₂| / (|n₁| |n₂|) = |a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ + c₁c₂| / [√(a₁²+b₁²+c₁²) √(a₂²+b₂²+c₂²)].
Perpendicular planes: a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ + c₁c₂ = 0. Parallel planes: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂.
Perpendicular distance from point P(x₁, y₁, z₁) to plane ax + by + cz + d = 0: p = |ax₁ + by₁ + cz₁ + d| / √(a² + b² + c²).
Distance between parallel planes ax + by + cz + d₁ = 0 and ax + by + cz + d₂ = 0: d = |d₁ − d₂| / √(a² + b² + c²).

formulas.label: Point to plane distance
formulas.expr: p = |ax₁ + by₁ + cz₁ + d| / √(a² + b² + c²)

nodes.title: Interaction Between Line and Plane
points: Angle θ between line r = a + λ b and plane r · n = d:
sinθ = |b · n| / (|b| |n|) = |a₁a + b₁b + c₁c| / [√(a₁²+b₁²+c₁²) √(a²+b²+c²)] (Notice sinθ, NOT cosθ!).
Line PARALLEL to plane: b ⊥ n ⟹ b · n = 0 ⟹ a a₁ + b b₁ + c c₁ = 0.
Line PERPENDICULAR to plane: b ∥ n ⟹ a/a₁ = b/b₁ = c/c₁.
Line lies ENTIRELY in plane: b · n = 0 AND point a satisfies plane equation (a · n = d).

formulas.label: Line parallel to plane
formulas.expr: b · n = 0 ⟹ a a₁ + b b₁ + c c₁ = 0

nodes.title: Coplanarity of Lines & Plane Containing Them
points: Two lines r = a₁ + λ b₁ and r = a₂ + μ b₂ are coplanar if and only if: (a₂ − a₁) · (b₁ × b₂) = 0.
Cartesian coplanarity condition: det [[x₂−x₁, y₂−y₁, z₂−z₁], [a₁, b₁, c₁], [a₂, b₂, c₂]] = 0.
Equation of plane containing both lines:
Vector form: (r − a₁) · (b₁ × b₂) = 0;
Cartesian form: det [[x−x₁, y−y₁, z−z₁], [a₁, b₁, c₁], [a₂, b₂, c₂]] = 0.

formulas.label: Plane containing lines
formulas.expr: det [[x−x₁, y−y₁, z−z₁], [a₁, b₁, c₁], [a₂, b₂, c₂]] = 0

nodes.title: Foot of Perpendicular & Image of Point
points: Foot of perpendicular (x, y, z) from point P(x₁, y₁, z₁) to plane ax + by + cz + d = 0:
(x − x₁)/a = (y − y₁)/b = (z − z₁)/c = −(ax₁ + by₁ + cz₁ + d) / (a² + b² + c²).
Image (reflection) of point P(x₁, y₁, z₁) in plane ax + by + cz + d = 0:
(x − x₁)/a = (y − y₁)/b = (z − z₁)/c = −2(ax₁ + by₁ + cz₁ + d) / (a² + b² + c²).
Foot of perpendicular on a line: write general point on line in parameter λ, dot product of line vector with PP' equals 0, solve for λ.

nodes.title: Must-Know Board Theorems & Proofs
points: Board Favourite #1: Theorem: Derive vector and Cartesian equation of a line passing through a point and parallel to a given vector: r = a + λ b.
Board Favourite #2: Theorem: Derive expression for shortest distance between two skew lines: d = |(a₂ − a₁) · (b₁ × b₂)| / |b₁ × b₂|.
Board Favourite #3: Theorem: Derive vector and Cartesian equation of a plane in normal form: r · n̂ = p.
Board Favourite #4: Theorem: Derive equation of a plane passing through a point and perpendicular to a given vector: (r − a) · n = 0.
Board Favourite #5: Find the foot of perpendicular and length of perpendicular from a point to a line/plane.

nodes.title: MHT-CET Angle Traps, Shortcuts & 10-Second Hacks
points: Angle Trap: Angle between Line and Plane is given by sinθ (NOT cosθ!). For parallel, dot product = 0; for perpendicular, cross product = 0.

Parallel Planes Distance Trap: Make sure coefficients of x, y, z are EXACTLY identical before applying |d₁ − d₂| / √(a² + b² + c²). If one equation is 2x + 4y + 4z = 6 and other is x + 2y + 2z = 5, divide first by 2!
10-Second Foot of Perpendicular: Use (x − x₁)/a = (y − y₁)/b = (z − z₁)/c = −k.
Intersection of Line and Plane: Substitute general point (x₁ + λa, y₁ + λb, z₁ + λc) directly into plane equation to solve for λ in 1 step.

formulas.label: Parallel planes trap check
formulas.expr: Ensure identical coefficients a, b, c
